obligations.note: Head commit 411570a changes required_approvals from `amount >= policy.DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD` to `amount > ...`. A payment of exactly 10,000.00 now needs only one approver, which violates the approved at-or-above dual-control rule.

approve() still refuses the creator and duplicate approvers, and is_fully_approved counts only distinct approvers. However, the registered control test test_maker_cannot_check ran only on 4655e99, not on the final commit, so the required exhaustive evidence is missing for head.

release() is textually unchanged and still returns the prior release from find_release before sending. Ledger entry ACR-0403 covers payments.py#release, whose behaviour is unchanged, so it still supports this obligation.

Ledger entry ACR-0401 (PAY-1 proof covering payments.py#required_approvals) has lapsed because required_approvals changed in behaviour. No new evidence of equal strength exists for head, and the proved property (`2 iff a >= threshold`) no longer holds.

Ticket CHG-24576 is standard and was approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-15, before review. Its components (payments.payments, payments.tests) cover payments.py and tests/test_approvals_remaining.py.
mara.costa@fernbrook.example gave a code_review approval. She holds change_approver for payments and is a different person from the author, Sofia Santos.
The code_review approval names the head commit 411570a56bdc, so it covers what would be merged.

The CI run.json is for commit 4655e99d, not head 411570a5. The later commit is a behavioural change (the threshold comparison), not comment or formatting, so the run does not count for the final commit. The JUnit timestamp (2026-10-23, from a personal Mac host) also does not match the run.
No exception in the register covers PAY-1 or payments.payments, so the dual-control deviation is not excused.

summary: The second commit, 'Simplify threshold check', changes required_approvals from >= to >. Payments of exactly 10,000.00 would then be released with a single approver, which violates PAY-1, and no exception covers the deviation. The existing PAY-1 proof has lapsed under LAP-1. The CI run was on the earlier commit, so CHG-4 is not met for the final commit. The change is rejected; restore the >= comparison and rerun the full suite, including the control tests, on the final commit.
